lines.text: If you rub wheat between two stones all day, you get one loaf and gorilla arms.
But everyone wants bread. So you put a round stone on top and spin it.
But your arm is dying. So you make the stones huge and tie on a donkey.
It walks in circles and flour pours out.
Congratulations! You just built the donkey mill.
But the donkey eats half your wheat.
So you hammer a giant post into the hill and nail four sails to it.
Now the wind turns your stones for free.
But the wind changes direction and your sails stop.
Being an absolute genius, you put the whole mill house on the post and push it round with a long tail pole.
Congratulations! You just built the post mill.
But a storm hits, the sails spin wildly, and the miller vanishes in flour.
So you clamp a brake on the big wheel, and it rubs so hard it smokes.
But you want bigger sails, and the house gets too heavy to push.
So you build a stone tower in its place, and only the small cap turns.
Congratulations! You just built the tower mill.
But one night the wind swings behind the sails and nearly rips the cap off.
Using your huge brain, you stick a tiny sideways windmill on the back of the cap.
When the wind shifts, it spins and cranks the cap back around by itself.
Congratulations! You just built the windmill, with Edmund Lee's fantail from seventeen forty-five.
